content:
After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to all users, bringing Apple's new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major new features for Safari, and a slew of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here's everything new.

At this year's WWDC, Apple introduced its operating systems in a way that was somewhat different from what users and developers had come to expect.

Rather than going platform by platform through new features, Apple spent relatively less time on each operating system, focusing the event on cross-platform features and improvements, largely because many of these features rely on the all-new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes several welcome first-party improvements in design and functionality, starting with some much-needed Liquid Glass adjustments.

Liquid Glass and interface improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 adopted Apple's bold new design, the visual treatment fell short compared to other systems, especially when stacked against iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

In the macOS 27 Golden Gate update, Apple has spent considerable time further integrating the new Liquid Glass throughout the system while bringing over select visual adjustments introduced in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Among them is a new Liquid Glass slider that lets users dial transparency up or down to their liking.

There's also a fun Easter egg tucked inside the Liquid Glass appearance settings: Clarus the Dogcow, who appears if you keep scrolling down past the demo pane.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also introduces redesigned app icons that better fit the Liquid Glass aesthetic, with more layers added for depth and detail across light, dark, tinted, and fully clear global system appearances.

The same goes for the redesigned traffic light buttons added during the beta period. The new design ditches the flat green, yellow, and red controls in favor of a Liquid Glass treatment, complete with a playful bounce effect when users click (or perhaps tap, soon?) and drag before releasing.

Another welcome interface refinement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple's decision to unify the corner radius of system windows and apps, rather than dynamically adjusting based on the UI elements in the window's menu bar.

Although Apple's original intent was deliberate, many people mistook the inconsistent corner radii for a bug, prompting Apple to call out the change specifically during its WWDC keynote.

Another equally controversial design decision sees macOS 27 Golden Gate drop the practice of displaying a slew of icons alongside menu items. In macOS 26 Tahoe, Apple added symbols next to nearly every command in almost every app, intended to make menus more scannable, but it was widely criticized for making menus more visually busy and harder to scan in certain situations.

Fortunately, with macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has reversed course and removed most of these icons, returning menus to a cleaner, more visually tidy appearance.

Other visual details in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and more pronounced active windows, both of which were controversial additions in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the new Siri app

This is arguably the biggest new feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple's rebuilt Siri, developed in partnership with Google's Gemini models, comes with its own standalone app and deep integration throughout the system.

The new Siri AI uses a new on-device indexing system to process user data, and it lives both in Spotlight and in the new Siri app.

The Siri app looks and operates largely like other AI assistant apps users are familiar with: a sidebar on the left lists chat history across all compatible platforms, while the main chat pane lets users enter prompts, attach images and files, or start voice conversations. The app also supports search and pinned conversations, which is a nice plus for users with different workflows.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and from the user's context to deliver practical, actionable answers. Throughout the beta, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive feedback, though it can sometimes feel a touch slow for users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants.

Another practical feature of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with native and third-party apps and carry out actions directly, taking the old Siri's app integration significantly further.

Crucially, developers need to expose their apps' content and functionality via the App Intents framework, so the experience here will continue to improve as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Finally, there's a universal 'Ask Siri' option in the right-click menu that lets users select text, images, or files and ask Siri directly. For example, users can Control-click an image in a document and ask Siri to help them learn more about it, or select a passage of text and ask Siri to rewrite it, proofread it, adjust the tone, or offer writing suggestions.

Siri AI launches with English support at launch, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish support coming in October. For now, Siri AI is unavailable in mainland China and the EU due to regulatory issues.

Apple Intelligence

We've previously covered Apple's new foundation models in depth, focusing on the new versions of the Apple Intelligence models Apple has developed for its 2027 operating systems. Here's how Apple describes each:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3 billion parameter dense model, delivers higher quality. AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most capable on-device model. It's natively multimodal, enabling more expressive voice and higher-accuracy dictation. Built on Apple's cutting-edge work, this 20 billion parameter model uses a sparse architecture, activating only 1 to 4 billion parameters on demand. AFM 3 Core Advanced is unlocked and optimized for our most powerful Apple Silicon systems. AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse, optimized for speed, efficiency, and capability. AFM 3 Cloud (Image), used for image generation and editing, unlocking advanced photo editing tools, a new Image Playground, and more. AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most capable server-side model, powering our most demanding use cases like agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate uses two on-device models—AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced—while the rest are cloud-based. The performance of these on-device models depends on the Mac's hardware, particularly the memory available to run the model's active parameters alongside other AI workloads.

When it comes to how Apple Intelligence is implemented in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the results are mixed. The models themselves are quite capable at everyday tasks, like helping draft messages, proofreading documents, or summarizing text.

The issue is that Apple is now somewhat over-emphasizing how and when Siri AI surfaces, which can occasionally feel overwhelming to users and even get in the way of what they were trying to do.

One standout new addition to Apple Intelligence in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new Visual Intelligence shortcut. With a press of Command-Shift-Space, users can select any area of the screen and immediately ask Siri about it. Images, PDFs, text, or basically anything on screen qualifies.

Unfortunately, not every Mac that supports macOS 27 will run the new Apple Intelligence—it requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here's the official list of Macs that Apple says support the new features:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
  • iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)
  • Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 and later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features support the same languages as the current version of Apple Intelligence, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in mainland China due to regulatory issues. Apple has also said there will be usage limits on some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features, but the company has not yet shared specifics.

Performance and stability improvements

At the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted countless improvements rolling out across all of its operating systems.

On macOS 27 Golden Gate, those improvements include faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (especially for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud photo uploads with selective priority sync.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves scrolling performance in Safari and Calendar, as well as animation in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple has also tuned indexing and search in Mail, along with the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other refinements include better consistency and persistence of window positions across external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, broader high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes for external displays, and improved Sidecar touch support, including tap controls, single-finger scrolling, system gestures, and markup features.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces Notify Me, a new Safari feature that can monitor web pages and alert users when relevant changes occur, such as price drops, restocks, event registration openings, or just about anything a user asks it to track.

Notify Me can check hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, with additional options to set the days and times it checks.

Additionally, Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces "describe extensions," which let users build extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples spanning productivity, focus, creativity, and design and development. Users can simply describe what they need in their own words, and Apple Intelligence handles the rest.

Both features are accessible from the 'More Options' hamburger menu on the right side of an active Safari tab.

For users who habitually end up with a mountain of open tabs, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs by topic.

Another fun new addition in Safari for macOS 27 Golden Gate is the pull-to-refresh gesture, which works just like on iOS and iPadOS—users can swipe down past the rubber band effect to refresh the page.

The gesture also works in other system apps like Mail, News, and Calendar, which many see as another sign of the rumored touchscreen Mac, expected to be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios, which many see as an early sign of Apple prepping the feature for a foldable iPhone.

Now that iPhone Duo has officially launched, Mac users can get an early taste of that experience. Unfortunately, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring is still unavailable in the EU.

Shortcuts

This is arguably one of the most useful Apple Intelligence additions in this year's OS updates.

While Shortcuts already offers a fairly approachable way to automate things, it can still feel daunting for average users. Now users simply describe what they want to accomplish, and Apple Intelligence builds it as a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights a few suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

  • Dictate and translate to Spanish
  • Write a haiku about the weather forecast
  • Play my workout playlist when I arrive at the gym
  • Make a recipe from these leftovers
  • Summarize my day each morning
  • Prioritize my to-do list each morning
  • Get directions when I get in the car
  • Dictate my thoughts and save them to the clipboard
  • Dim the screen when bedtime begins
  • Turn on Do Not Disturb when I open the TV app

As an aside, if you want to dive deeper into Shortcuts, be sure to follow Stephen Robles' excellent work on YouTube and Instagram. Also check out Shortcuts Playground from MacStories, a more powerful natural language-based shortcut builder.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three Apple Intelligence-powered editing tools: an enhanced Clean Up, which can remove objects, people, or other unwanted elements from photos; Extend, which can generate areas around a photo when the original was cropped too tightly; and Spatial Reframing, which lets users change the angle and composition of a photo after the fact.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now support full-resolution sharing and let Windows and Android users join via iCloud.com.

Other new features include the ability to play any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transitions, and duration; a new star rating system for rating photos; and a brand new "Shot by Me" dedicated collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate details

  • Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.
  • Finder can now intelligently suggest names based on the contents of files and folders.
  • Image Playgrounds has expanded style support and uses a new foundation model for better results.
  • The Flyover experience in Maps has been enhanced, with sharper textures, details, and rendering for hundreds of cities worldwide.
  • Messages finally integrates tap-back notifications and has improved cross-device syncing.
  • Notes supports handwritten notes and sketches via trackpad, expands Markdown support through copy and paste, and adds section links.
  • Podcasts now supports video podcasts with picture-in-picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final version to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, "after installing this update, only apps will no longer be able to run on Mac computers with Apple silicon," and you can learn more here.

Compatibility

According to Apple's official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Macs:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)

What's your favorite new feature? Let us know in the comments.
